title: US stocks fall as oil surges past $100 on deepening Middle East tensions | Stock Market News
text:
US stock markets fell on Waednesday as oil prices surged past the market-sensitive $100-a-barrel mark for the first time since July as Middle East tensions escalated further. At the open, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 78.2 points, or 0.15%, to 52,707.9. The S&P 500 fell 12.8 points, or 0.17%, to 7,660.68​, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 96.4 points, or 0.36%, to 26,325.061. Brent futures were trading above $101 a barrel on escalations in the US-Iran war as Iran responded to US attacks that destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they attacked two US vessels, eight oil tankers, and 10 "non-compliant vessels" that were trying to pass through the strait, Iranian state media reported. Futures markets have now placed about 60% odds that the US Federal Reserve will lift interest rates later this month.
